answer: No head acts until an anchor has watched it for twice the epochs of the earlier head of the same root, and only once every mirror of the ledger shows it, so a new wallet from that root lands in the same tally. Anchors are paid a measure of timber per epoch: an honest newcomer pays one measure for one epoch, while an operator running a thousand identities must have its last head watched 2^999 epochs and pay 2^1000 measures of timber in all.
